newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese minister says army can impose curfew.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese minister says army can impose curfew.

text.p: Lebanon's interior minister said on Wednesday an opposition demonstration planned to take place during a general strike on Thursday was banned and the army had the authority to impose a curfew if necessary.
Michel al-Murr, who is also deputy prime minister, told reporters it was up to the army and security forces to maintain security.

Questioned by reporters in parliament during a confidence debate on the government, Murr did not say specifically that troops would be used to prevent the demonstration, called in protest at government policies on media and social issues.
"There is a previous decision taken by the government banning demonstrations and this decision is still valid today," Murr said.
"The task of the army and security forces is to maintain security in the country and they take the measures needed for this task," he added.

Asked whether the army might impose a curfew, as it did last February to prevent a planned demonstration during a general strike, Murr said: "This is not our responsibility....If the army found that the situation needed a curfew declaration, it could do so."
